case_name: Union of India and Others v K. P. Prabhakaran
respondent:
K. P. Prabhakaran
Supreme Court of India

27 November 1996
C.As. Nos. 1364 and 1365 of 1979
The Order of the Court was as follows:
1. These appeals by the Union of India relate to appointment on the posts of Enquiry-cum-Reservation Clerks in the four metropolitan cities of Madras, Bombay, Calcutta and Delhi. In April 1978 the Railway Administration took a decision tbat both the upper and lower class reservation counters in the Reservation Offices in the metropolitan cities of a Madras, Bombay, Calcutta and Delhi would have to be manned only by women. By circular dated 30-6-1978, it was decided that the Reservation Offices in the said metropolitan cities should constitute seniority unit separate from the rest of the Enquiry and Reservation cadre in the Railways. By the impugned judgment, the Madras High Court has quashed the said circular dated 30-6-1978 on the view that it was violative of provisions of Arts. 14 and 16(1) and (2) of the Constitution.
2. The
facts: The Railway Administration took a decision in April 1978 that both the upper and lower class reservation counters in the Reservation Offices in the metropolitan cities of Madras, Bombay, Calcutta and Delhi would have to be manned only by women.

By circular dated 30-6-1978, it was decided that the Reservation Offices in the said metropolitan cities should constitute seniority unit separate from the rest of the Enquiry and Reservation cadre in the Railways.
The Madras High Court has quashed the said circular dated 30-6-1978 on the view that it was violative of provisions of Arts. 14 and 16(1) and (2) of the Constitution.
issues: Whether Art. 15(3) can be read as a proviso or an exception qualifying or restricting the guarantee under arts. 16(1) and (2) of the Constitution
respondent_arguments: The impugned judgment of the High Court holding that Art. 15(3) has no application in matters relating to employment under the State falling u/arts. 16(1) and (2) cannot be upheld
court_reasoning: Art. 15 deals with every kind of State action in relation to the citizens of this country and that every sphere of activity of the State is controlled by Art. 15(1) and, therefore, there was no reason to exclude from the ambit of Art. 15(1) employment under the State.
Since Arts. 15(1) and 15(3) go together, the protection of Art. 15(3) would be applicable to employment under the State falling u/arts. 16(1) and (2) of the Constitution.
holding: The appeals are disposed of accordingly.
